title: mmz status
description: Output of `mmz --status=json`: each rule's freshness against its cache.

manifest.description: Path of the manifest governing the working directory.

probes.description: Each probe mmz resolved for this report, name to the lowercase hex blake3 of its stdout — what mmz actually saw. A declared probe that no reported rule names in its inputs is never run, so it is absent here. Absent entirely when the report named none.

rules.description: One entry per command rule, in manifest order.

name.description: The rule's name (matcher and cache identity).

source.description: The file that declared this rule: project-root-relative when it is under the project root, absolute otherwise (so a fragment outside the project, a Nix store path say, stays recognisable). Present for every rule, including in a single-file project with no `imports:` — the root manifest is the source of its own rules, not a special case.

state.description: Freshness verdict. `fresh`: cache hit. `stale`: inputs changed — a file, or a probe whose stdout moved. `never`: no record yet. `failed`: last run failed, so it re-runs. `no-inputs`: the rule resolves to zero files and names no probe. `missing-output`: a declared output is gone, so the record is void whatever the inputs hash — it outranks `stale`, since an input change is the assumption a reader already holds.

digest.description: Digest of the current inputs — its resolved files folded with the digest of every probe it names. Absent when the rule resolves to no files and names no probe.

missing_output.description: The declared output that voided the record, as the manifest spells it (the first one missing, in declaration order). Present exactly when state is `missing-output`.

cached.description: The stored record. Absent when the rule has never run.

digest.description: Input digest recorded at the last run.

ran_at.description: Unix seconds when the record was written.

outputs.description: The outputs the rule declared when this run was recorded, so a missing one is reported against the run that promised it. Absent when the rule declared none.

probes.description: The digest each named probe produced when this run was recorded, so it can be diffed against the report's top-level `probes` — which is how a stale verdict names the probe that moved rather than sending a reader to diff files that did not. Absent when the rule named none.

inputs.description: Resolved inputs with content hashes, sorted by path.

path.description: Path relative to the manifest root, forward slashes.

hash.description: Lowercase hex blake3 of the file's contents.
